items.title: The Lynx XM30 is making its case to be the US Army’s Bradley replacement
items.originalTitle: The Lynx XM30 is making its case to be the US Army’s Bradley replacement
items.summary: American Rheinmetall , one of two defense companies chosen to develop replacements for the Army’s M2 Bradley Fighting Vehicle , announced in September the delivery of its Lynx XM30 prototype to the service. The Army conducted initial safety tests before allowing soldiers to join the trial-and-error phase. “Now it’s in soldiers’ hands,” said Chris Haag, vice president of business development and strategy at Rheinmetall.

evidenceRecords.text: American Rheinmetall , one of two defense companies chosen to develop replacements for the Army’s M2 Bradley Fighting Vehicle , announced in September the delivery of its Lynx XM30 prototype to the service.
The Army conducted initial safety tests before allowing soldiers to join the trial-and-error phase.
“Now it’s in soldiers’ hands,” said Chris Haag, vice president of business development and strategy at Rheinmetall.

“Seeing their eyes light up when they got to see the vehicle for the first time is pretty awesome.” While Haag could not disclose where soldiers were along the tinkering process, he confirmed that service members were in possession of the vehicle and were at least able to hop inside and turn it on, beginning a new era for Army combat vehicles.

Rheinmetall is currently competing for the XM30 Army contract with General Dynamics Land Systems, which is unveiling its Wolf XM30 prototype at the Association of the U.S. Army Annual Meeting and Exposition in Washington, D.C., from Oct. 12 to 14.
The Army selected the companies in 2023 for the design phase of a process that will eventually replace the Bradley, which arrived in the 1980s.
The Lynx XM30 is designed for modern combat environments riddled with drones and electronic warfare, like those seen in Ukraine.
The vehicle will wield a hybrid-electric powertrain and an uncrewed 50mm turret, providing more firepower than the Bradley, which boasts a 25mm M242 Bushmaster.

American Rheinmetall’s prototype likely wouldn’t differ from General Dynamics’ XM30 design when it came to physical architecture, Haag said, which meant the Lynx could differentiate itself from competition through aspects like power, engine, transmission and soldiers’ experience with user interface and operability in general.

For large modernization efforts, the M2 Bradley Fighting Vehicle may have to travel back to an Army or manufacturing facility to undergo overhauls or block upgrades, whereas the XM30 could potentially undergo software updates that revamp the system in a much shorter timeframe and require less geographical displacement.

The company will deliver seven more prototypes to the Army by the end of the year, all part of a nearly $764 million Engineering and Manufacturing Development contract to expand the XM30 from digital design through validation.

The company will continue bringing its ElliQ AI companion to aging New Yorkers at risk of loneliness and social isolation.
With the expansion, NYSOFA and Intuition Robotics created a new three-year, $2.1 million agreement.
The expansion builds on the organizations’ three years of experience working together.
During that time, ElliQ has demonstrated its ability to reduce loneliness and improve health and wellbeing.
The robot also helps older adults remain healthier and more independent in their own homes.

“Loneliness and isolation are commonly heard today, but make no mistake, the health effects are devastating, and NYSOFA is working continuously to provide the help older New Yorkers need,” said Greg Olsen, director of the office .

“ElliQ is an essential tool to help combat the loneliness epidemic, joining dozens of other projects launched by NYSOFA to overcome the digital divide, address social isolation, improve health and wellness, and support caregivers.” NYSOFA established its first public-private partnership in 2018, following a report by AARP and the U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) on the impact of loneliness and social isolation on older adults and Medicare spending.
It stated that loneliness and isolation are equivalent to smoking almost a pack of cigarettes per day, cost Medicare more than $7 billion to treat, and make chronic conditions worse.
In addition to its partnership with NYSOFA, Intuition Robotics has similar partnerships in Wisconsin, Florida, and Washington.
In Washington, the program is aimed at Medicaid recipients .

“This partnership extension continues our long term partnership with the state of New York, and its Office for the Aging, reflecting three years of measurable, record-breaking engagement results: older adults across New York are engaging with ElliQ more often, feeling less lonely, and staying more connected to the people who matter to them,” said Dor Skuler, co-founder and CEO of Intuition Robotics.

evidenceRecords.text: In September, however, Gulf oil flows through Hormuz, excluding Iran, recovered to more than 81 percent of pre-war levels, while crude exports from the wider Middle East exceeded pre-war levels on 14 days during the month, Kpler reported.
Shepherded by the US Navy, more and more oil tankers had started passing through.

The Iranian threat meant ship crew were being paid hefty bonuses, insurance rates remained very high, and some analysts suspect that Gulf nations may also have been paying off Iran to allow tankers to transit.
This means that while more oil was being exported from the region, crude prices remained high.
But the surge in Iranian attacks in recent days has changed the equation.
According to Kpler, only 2.9 million barrels of oil were carried through the waterway on October 11, the lowest level this month.
As recently as October 8, nearly 20.8 million barrels of oil passed through the strait.
The pre-war average was 17.1 million barrels a day.
Oil prices continued to climb on Wednesday morning, with Brent crude futures gaining 89 cents, or 0.8 percent, to $106.58 a barrel as of 00:30 GMT.
Brent futures had closed at $105.69 a barrel on Tuesday, while West Texas Intermediate settled at $94.14.
On Wednesday, a US military official confirmed to Reuters that Iran had changed tactics in the Strait of Hormuz in one significant way.

Since Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz after the war began, the US Navy has reportedly opened up a route so Gulf states can export oil and other commodities amid the energy crisis caused by Iran’s attacks on ships.

The president's move to address the rapid development of the AI industry came after he met with top AI executives at the end of September — and a month before midterm elections in November.
Trump has faced intensifying pressure and warnings from business and political leaders about the mostly unregulated technology.
The name echoes Trump's September executive order renaming "Artificial Intelligence" as "Super intelligence" (SI).
Jay Clayton, the director of national security and the president's new AI czar, is the task force leader.

The task force will coordinate the government's effort "to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence," Trump said, and "will protect the interests, and improve the lives, of all Americans."
Trump has made it clear he does not want regulation to "stifle" progress in the SI industry, and a reported charter for the group says it will work to prevent "overregulation and regulatory capture."
The White House has not released any information about the Super Intelligence Force, but a copy of a charter detailing the group's responsibilities was reported in The Wall Street Journal
Clayton, whom Trump named AI czar in early October, is to chair the task force.

He told The Wall Street Journal he expected AI mechanisms to be "developed in dialogue," citing risk models the Securities and Exchange Commission, which he headed during Trump's first presidential term, and the Federal Reserve developed for the financial industry.
Key members of Trump's Cabinet, including Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, are also on the task force.

evidenceRecords.text: Beirut, Lebanon – Ali is from Khiam, a Lebanese village on the southern border with Israel, but for the last few months he has rented a house in Hasbaiyya, about a half-hour drive away to the northeast.
He is one of tens of thousands of Lebanese who have been displaced from their homes in villages throughout the south of the country.
Israel responded by intensifying its war on Lebanon for a second time in under two years.
Israeli attacks, as well as its reinvasion of southern Lebanon, displaced more than 1.2 million people.
Since then, Beirut has entered into US-brokered direct negotiations with the Israeli government, despite the objections of Hezbollah, which has fought Israel since October 2023.
The group traces its origins in the 1980s to resistance against Israeli occupation of Lebanese territory.
Israel currently occupies a zone stretching up to 10 kilometres (6.2 miles) deep into southern Lebanon.
Behind the “Yellow Line” that marks the end of that occupation zone, Israel continues to detonate homes.
Israel uses the same “Yellow Line” term to refer to the areas it controls in Gaza.

“Israel’s primary goals were to empty, depopulate, and make those dozens of frontline villages and towns uninhabitable, and we’ve seen that now with the satellite imagery,” Mohamad Bazzi, a New York-based political analyst originally from Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon, told Al Jazeera. “It was a way of applying that Gaza model to Lebanon.”

“[The Yellow Line] is treated as a hard boundary, both in terms of troop presence and the controlled demolition of villages, which continues unabated despite the ceasefire,” Ahmad Baydoun, a Lebanese architect and open-source researcher based in the Netherlands, told Al Jazeera. “It is as if the ceasefire applies to the rest of Lebanon but not to this territory.”
The Yellow Line is not the only coloured line used in Lebanon to reference military demarcations.

“Israel’s primary goals were to empty, depopulate, and make those dozens of frontline villages and towns uninhabitable, and we’ve seen that now with the satellite imagery,” Mohamad Bazzi, a New York-based political analyst originally from Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon, told Al Jazeera.
The Blue Line was established in 2000 in the wake of the end of Israel’s years-long occupation of southern Lebanon, with Israeli forces withdrawing behind it.

“Part of the Israeli strategy here with the Grey Line, Blue Line, Yellow Line is to sow confusion and to hide or obfuscate the reality of what Israel has done on the ground [which is] to depopulate this vast Lebanese territory and to make it uninhabitable,” Bazzi, the analyst, said.

We’ve seen that play out in Gaza, and the bottom line is Israel is illegally occupying and has illegally destroyed and ethnically cleansed a huge part of southern Lebanon, and the world sat silent while that happened for the most part.”
But even within the area on the Israeli-controlled side of the Yellow Line, some villagers remain, reflecting Israeli attempts to play on Lebanon’s sectarian divides.

items.originalTitle: US Army suspends longtime hometown recruiter assistance program, faces cancellation
items.summary: The service’s decades-old Hometown Recruiter Assistance Program has been suspended, Lt. Gen. Johnny Davis confirmed at a forum hosted by the Association of the United States Army. “I would tell you, when the program was initiated and really delivered to the Army years ago and executed, that we had some good return on investment — about, you know, one or two percent,” Davis said in response to a question at the forum.

evidenceRecords.text: The service’s decades-old Hometown Recruiter Assistance Program has been suspended, Lt.
Army recruiting social media pages began discussing the suspension of the Hometown Recruiter Assistance Program in January, though the service has not publicly addressed the move until now.
The service’s decades-old Hometown Recruiter Assistance Program has been suspended, Lt. Gen. Johnny Davis confirmed at a forum hosted by the Association of the United States Army.

“I would tell you, when the program was initiated and really delivered to the Army years ago and executed, that we had some good return on investment — about, you know, one or two percent,” Davis said in response to a question at the forum.
Davis said leaders understood the “human element” of what was happening, in that new graduates were eager to reconnect with family and friends in what amounted to additional uncharged leave.
But, he added, the Army had to consider what it was getting out of the arrangement.

Likewise, he said, the Army has in the past allowed National Guard and Reserve soldiers to return home for non-charged leave during the holiday break known as the Christmas Exodus on the understanding that they would support Army recruiting as ambassadors during that time.
“During that Christmas holiday, was there a lot of recruiters in the recruiting stations working with them?
No,” Davis said. “So we’re really thinking through: is this return on investment, and is it worth the cost to the Army?
Or can we take those funds and spend them in other ways to help our men and women.”
Davis said leaders were now “looking at other ways” to help soldiers get coveted hometown leave apart from the hometown recruiting program.
In a 2022 Army news release, a recruiting center station commander in Missouri, Staff Sgt.
Colton Dunbar, said the success of the program came down to “how the soldiers are leveraged.”

items.summary: Researchers at Columbia University, Google DeepMind, and Google published a technical paper titled “Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification.” Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have made rapid inroads into Electronic Design Automation (EDA), approximately 74.6% of existing studies target static Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code generation, leaving post-simulation verification and interactive waveform debugging largely untouched.

evidenceRecords.text: Researchers at Columbia University, Google DeepMind , and Google published a technical paper titled “Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification.” Abstract “The unprecedented computational scale of modern artificial intelligence depends on complex, multi-billion-transistor Systems-on-Chip, yet the workflows that verify these chips remain stubbornly manual.

Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have made rapid inroads into Electronic Design Automation (EDA), approximately 74.6% of existing studies target static Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code generation, leaving post-simulation verification and interactive waveform debugging largely untouched.

BTTF distills massive, unstructured simulation dumps into a normalized relational SQLite database and couples it with a collaborative multi-agent orchestration engine that translates natural-language verification queries into schema-aware SQL while correlating signal anomalies with versioned RTL repositories.
Across a 150-query benchmark, BTTF attains 95.33% execution accuracy, charting a practical path toward autonomous EDA verification.” Find the technical paper here .

evidenceRecords.text: Facebook is the latest social media platform to give users greater control over the algorithm that determines what appears in their feeds.
Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” on Tuesday, a feature it first launched on Instagram.
The new tool allows Facebook users to influence the content they see in Feed and Reels by describing their preferences in their own words using natural language.
Rather than relying entirely on automated recommendations, users can now communicate directly with the platform about the topics and content they want to see more or less frequently.
According to Meta, the feature is designed to make content recommendations more relevant.
Users can adjust their preferences and interact with the algorithms responsible for ranking and recommending posts, with changes reflected in their recommendations in real time.
The company has also updated Facebook’s three-dot menu, making it easier for users to manage their content preferences directly from individual posts.
By opening the menu, users can access “Your Algorithm” or select the “Interested” and “Not interested” options to indicate whether particular content aligns with their preferences.
Meta says the platform may ask follow-up questions to better understand what users liked or disliked, allowing them to provide more detailed feedback.
Users can explain what they want to see more or less of, helping Facebook refine its recommendations based on their responses.
The introduction of “Your Algorithm” reflects Meta’s broader effort to give people more influence over their social media experiences as AI increasingly shapes content discovery.

The move signals a shift away from the traditional recommendation systems that have shaped social media experiences for years, bringing the platform closer to streaming services that allow users to personalize recommendations based on their interests and preferences.
Instagram introduced Your Algorithm in June, extending customization options across Feed and Explore after first launching the feature for Reels in December 2025.

items.summary: The global race to stop hostile drones is turning into big business for defense contractors. Raytheon, an RTX company, has secured $729 million in contracts to supply components of its counter-drone system to the US Army, Qatar, and Jordan, marking the first international sales of two key technologies used in the system. The deals cover Raytheon’s Low, slow, small, uncrewed aircraft Integrated Defeat System, better known as LIDS.

evidenceRecords.text: The global race to stop hostile drones is turning into big business for defense contractors.

Raytheon, an RTX company, has secured $729 million in contracts to supply components of its counter-drone system to the US Army, Qatar, and Jordan, marking the first international sales of two key technologies used in the system.
The deals cover Raytheon’s Low, slow, small, uncrewed aircraft Integrated Defeat System, better known as LIDS.
The system combines radar and other detection technologies with interceptors designed to take down hostile drones before they can threaten military personnel, installations, or other critical assets.
At the heart of the system are two products: the Ku-band Radio Frequency Sensor (KuRFS) and the Coyote interceptor.
While KuRFS helps detect and track incoming threats across a 360-degree field of view, Coyote is designed to engage individual drones as well as coordinated swarms.
The Coyote family includes kinetic and non-kinetic effectors, giving military operators different ways to counter aerial threats.

Raytheon says the system’s interceptors have already achieved hundreds of intercepts in combat, providing an operational track record as militaries look for more effective ways to defend against increasingly common drone attacks.
The new contracts include both fixed-site and mobile LIDS configurations, allowing customers to deploy counter-drone defenses in different operational environments.
What’s particularly notable about the deal is the international expansion of KuRFS and Coyote.
Both technologies have been key elements of the US Army’s LIDS program, but these contracts represent their first international sales.
The agreements could help Raytheon expand its footprint in a market where demand for counter-drone capabilities is growing.

items.summary: Insider Brief Coinbase urged early preparation for Bitcoin’s transition to quantum-resistant security, citing the years needed to update network rules and migrate funds. The company called for evaluating signature systems that balance security, transaction costs, wallet usability and institutional custody requirements. Coinbase said debates over dormant or inaccessible coins should proceed alongside technical work so they do not delay quantum-resistant protections.

evidenceRecords.text: Insider Brief Coinbase urged early preparation for Bitcoin’s transition to quantum-resistant security, citing the years needed to update network rules and migrate funds.
The company called for evaluating signature systems that balance security, transaction costs, wallet usability and institutional custody requirements.
Coinbase said debates over dormant or inaccessible coins should proceed alongside technical work so they do not delay quantum-resistant protections.
In a blog post outlining its technical priorities , the cryptocurrency exchange and custodian said protecting Bitcoin will require more than selecting a new digital signature system.
The transition must also work for ordinary wallets and institutional custody, limit demands on the network and address funds whose owners cannot or will not move them.
Changes to Bitcoin’s shared rules and the movement of funds across its ecosystem can take years making advance preparation important even before the threat becomes certain, according to the post.
The company said it holds about 5% of all bitcoin in existence, giving it a substantial stake in how the network approaches the problem.

It is preparing its own systems, holding discussions with Bitcoin developers and researchers, and supporting open-source work through engineering resources and participation in the Bitcoin Security Consortium.
The post is an input to an open discussion rather than a final Coinbase position, the company said, ading that it does not establish a migration deadline or announce an agreed Bitcoin upgrade.
Coinbase’s main recommendation is to keep technical preparations moving while the community debates what should happen to abandoned or inaccessible coins.
In our view, that discussion can continue alongside the technical work to add post-quantum signature support to Bitcoin.” More Than a New Signature Digital signatures authorize bitcoin spending.
The potential threat described by Coinbase is a quantum computer powerful enough to defeat the cryptography behind existing signatures.

items.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
items.originalTitle: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
items.summary: Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, the brain implant company, explained onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how the company’s work with PRIMA fits into its broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface (BCI). “The retina is part of the central nervous system,” Hodak said.

evidenceRecords.text: Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision.

Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, the brain implant company, explained onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how the company’s work with PRIMA fits into its broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
“The retina is part of the central nervous system,” Hodak said. “We consider cochlear implants, retinal prostheses, motor prostheses, these are all different types of BCIs.”
Hodak outlined a vision in which BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications, rather than simply being a way to control computers.

While PRIMA is commercially available in Europe for patients who’ve lost their sight to geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases, including Stargardt disease, which is currently considered incurable.
Stargardt disease affects the outer retina, causing the gradual death of the eye’s light-sensing cells while potentially sparing the inner retina, the part that passes visual signals onto the brain.
It causes a central blind spot that gradually enlarges over time.
Approximately 150,000 people worldwide have lost vision due to the disease.

“One of the nice things about this device approach, when I was saying the brain’s a computer, vision is electrical potential, like electrical activity down the optic nerve,” Hodak said. “That’s all vision is to the brain, and so if you can get the optic nerve to signal the rest of the brain correctly, then you can provide vision to it.”
The company says its first patient with Stargardt disease received the PRIMA implant in May as part of its ongoing trial at the Sydney Eye Hospital in Australia.
During the patient’s first rehabilitation session, he saw a letter, and during the second, he was able to read a word.
To use the device, patients undergo an hourlong procedure that plants a small chip in the back of their eye, where the photoreceptors have degenerated.
“The retina is part of the central nervous system,” Hodak said.
“One of the nice things about this device approach, when I was saying the brain’s a computer, vision is electrical potential, like electrical activity down the optic nerve,” Hodak said.

items.summary: General Atomics Aeronautical Systems (GA-ASI) and Hanwha Aerospace completed operations in a simulated battlefield scenario with the Mojave short take-off and landing (STOL) drone on September 16. The testing formed part of a Defense Drone Technology Exhibition and included Mojave operating from an austere short runway at the Seungjin Training Field in Pocheon-si. The flying portion of the trials also saw the Mojave operating down at low level to demonstrate its ability to terrain mask to avoid potential threats and to support ground forces at close quarters.

items.title: Here's how to find the learning strategy that makes AI work for you
items.originalTitle: Here's how to find the learning strategy that makes AI work for you
items.summary: You are in charge when you use AI, so it's a good idea to come up with a learning strategy that works. Understanding this matters because successfully completing a task is not the same as learning from it. AI might help a person produce the right answer today without increasing their ability to independently produce a correct answer tomorrow. Language learning provides a useful example. An app such as Duolingo can provide structure, repetition and motivation.

evidenceRecords.text: You are in charge when you use AI, so it's a good idea to come up with a learning strategy that works.
Understanding this matters because successfully completing a task is not the same as learning from it.
AI might help a person produce the right answer today without increasing their ability to independently produce a correct answer tomorrow.
Language learning provides a useful example.
An app such as Duolingo can provide structure, repetition and motivation.

A learner can deepen that experience by trying to produce the answer from memory before looking at or selecting the options provided by the app, repeating unfamiliar sentences aloud or revisiting difficult vocabulary.
Deliberately retrieving information can improve longer-term retention compared with simply studying material again.
A large language model such as ChatGPT can play a different role.
It can explain things, compare sentence structures, generate further examples or help investigate something the learner has noticed.
When an app is used together with a large language model, they can create a richer learning ecosystem.

A small case study involving Duolingo users, for example, found that adding reflective journaling—writing down thoughts and goals—gave learners opportunities to articulate their strategies, difficulties and developing awareness of their own learning.
Consider two people using the same AI model.
Schools and universities can make learning itself more explicit, helping students understand why strategies such as retrieval, reflection and feedback work.
Here's how to find the learning strategy that makes AI work for you (2026, October 13)

Jordan warned about the reckless overuse of the term AI back in 2019. "I wasn't the only one saying it.
It was obvious that it would create the hysteria we're seeing now," he says. "You've seen what happened: AI wasn't enough, so they started talking about AGI, and now it's 'superintelligence'..."

evidenceRecords.text: This framework provides a simple physical interpretation of mode veering, complex mode formation, eigenvalue coalescence, and decay-rate splitting in lightly damped structural systems.
Why Complex Modes Can Appear at Low Damping Classical modal analysis often treats lightly damped structures as nearly proportional systems with real mode shapes.
That interpretation can become misleading when two modes are closely spaced.
In modal coordinates, nonproportional damping introduces an off-diagonal coupling term ε.
Reduced Perturbation Framework For a closely spaced pair, define the central eigenvalue λ0 ≈-ζω +iω and write the coupled eigenvalues as λ1,2=λ0 ±s.
This single relation determines the direction of eigenvalue separation in the complex plane, as summarized in Figure.
For 0 Engineering Interpretation and Recommended Practice Complexity in an identified mode shape should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of heavy damping, nonlinearity, or poor test data.
For a close modal pair, examine the complex poles together with mode-shape phase.

Frequency convergence accompanied by near-quadrature modal components is consistent with the imaginary-s regime; nearly equal frequencies accompanied by decay-rate separation is consistent with the real-s regime.
The framework also provides a practical testanalysis bridge: s=(λ1 -λ2 )/2 can be obtained from identified poles, while δ can be estimated from the uncoupled or pretest analytical modal spacing.

Horton, which will use its Factory-as-a-Service capabilities to produce more than 1,250 homes in the U.S. “Homebuilding has long lacked the production infrastructure needed to scale with the speed, predictability, and efficiency of modern manufacturing,” stated Ramtin Attar, co-founder and CEO of Promise Robotics.
“Physical AI changes that by creating a new production model that can expand capacity within and across markets.

Our goal is to make that capability accessible to builders across North America and support the industry’s long-term growth.” “We started the company on the central thesis that robotics for the homebuilding space needed a very different approach and tech stack,” he told The Robot Report .

“We started with mechanical and HVAC, and w’ve built the physical AI infrastructure for building component manufacturing.” Founded in 2021, Promise Robotics said it has integrated robotics, AI , software, and manufacturing systems to connect the homebuilding workflow, from design translation and production planning through automated manufacturing and onsite installation.

The Toronto-based company claimed that its Factory-as-a-Service (FaaS) model enables homebuilders to access advanced production infrastructure without the cost, complexity, or risk of developing and operating it themselves.

Construction needs to be more repeatable As construction firms navigate persistent housing demand , labor shortages, rising costs, and pressure to increase output, they are searching for more repeatable and scalable ways to expand production, said Promise Robotics.
“Unlike traditional manufacturing, especially automotive , where there are five or six big players, the construction industry is large but fragmented,” explained Attar.
“The workforce for homebuilding is also highly fragmented between businesses that manage the land, consumer houses, and seasonal trades.
